To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) pigeons can form classes of responses, (2) these classes can be expanded to include additional responses, and (3) the classes are not necessarily restricted to the responses used to form them.

(a) the response membership hypothesis is consistent with the results of the symmetry and class expansion test, and (b) these results provide evidence for response membership in pigeons’ stimulus-class formation.
the side-key response that is reinforced in the presence of a particular sample becomes a member of the same stimulus class as the sample and, in turn, the class of the sample.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of equivalence classes in the pigeon.
the question of whether a stimulus class is a collection of stimuli or a collection of stimuli and responses.
the question of what it is that pigeons learn during successive matching-to-sample training.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pigeons' stimulus classes are formed by the formation of equivalence classes and that the equivalence relations are formed by the establishment of symmetry relations.
response membership in stimulus-classes has been demonstrated. (Contains 4 tables and 4 figures.)
response membership in stimulus-class formation has been demonstrated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stimulus-class membership can be acquired by both stimuli and responses.
response membership in stimulus-class formation is not only possible but also a natural part of stimulus-class formation.
pigeons' stimulus classes are not just stimulus classes but are response classes as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
response membership in classes is not a theoretical construct but can be demonstrated in the laboratory.
response membership in stimulus equivalence classes can be demonstrated in a variety of ways.
the response membership hypothesis can account for the results of symmetry and class expansion probes in the context of a modified AB/BA symmetry test.
